steps.text: Fetch the EIA Midwest diesel series and save the raw data
steps.do: 1) Use fetch_url on the EIA API v2 URL for series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG (DEMO_KEY, weekly, sorted by period descending, length 60). If that fails, use the dnav history page https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG&f=W. 2) Read the whole response. Write the 60 newest week/price pairs to raw_eia.txt with the Write tool, passing the path explicitly. 3) Note the URL, today's retrieval date and the newest week seen. Do not fabricate any value.
steps.output: raw_eia.txt with at least 52 week/price pairs, plus a note giving the URL, retrieval date and newest week
steps.done_when: raw_eia.txt exists and holds at least 52 dated weekly prices copied from the fetched EIA response, or the failure is explained.

steps.text: Build weekly_prices.csv from the saved raw data
steps.do: 1) Read raw_eia.txt with local:Read, giving the path. 2) Take the 52 latest weeks and check they are 7 days apart and that the newest is the latest EIA release. 3) Write weekly_prices.csv with the Write tool, columns week_ending, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date, 52 rows. 4) In the reply give the retrieval date next to each web figure, name the series, and note that EIA has no Indiana-only series, so Midwest (PADD 2) is the proxy.
steps.output: table: weekly_prices.csv (week_ending x price_usd_per_gal x series_id x source_url x retrieved_date), 52 rows, plus a dated note on the latest week and the series name
steps.done_when: weekly_prices.csv exists with 52 consecutive weekly rows, each with date, price, series ID, source URL and retrieved_date, and the note states the retrieval date and the Midwest proxy.
